chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymoun, from Yahya ibn Talha, from Sawrah ibn Kuleyb, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the least of what would suffice from the Tashahhud, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The two testimonies'.

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: The act of testifying, specifically the recitation of testimonies during prayer
key_terms.الشَّهَادَتَانِ: The two testimonies (La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur Rasulullah)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of Tashahhud required to validly complete the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the minimum valid component of the Tashahhud, with Imam al-Baqir (AS) confirming that the two testimonies (Shahadatayn) suffice for the prayer to be valid. This ruling provides the foundational basis for the concise form of Tashahhud recited in the first and final Rak'ats, emphasizing the centrality of declaring Allah's oneness and the Prophethood of Muhammad (PBUH) as the core essence of the testimony during Salah.
